sourceCorrections: Three original assertions are corrected rather than adopted: typical HLA regional frequency, the shared HLA cytoband and frequency wording, and the superseded current TMB criterion. Original assertions remain explicit in the requirement proofs.

withheldRequirements.requirement: Region by region a tumour region typically had all three loci lost or none (page wording).
withheldRequirements.unitsOrInterpretiveLimit: Only partly supported: the PCR validation chose regions predicted all-loci or no-loci, so the claim is a selection property, not an observed frequency.
withheldRequirements.versionHandling: present in both versions; section signatures for the teaching sections of this requirement unchanged (later version differences are navigation metadata and cross-links only, see source-reading.json)

original.passage: In 90 non-small-cell lung cancers, the LOHHLA method found HLA LOH in 36 (40%); in the tumors examined region by region, a region typically had either all three loci lost or none ([McGranahan 2017](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5720478/)). Breast-cancer frequencies need their own studies.

A loss may occur in only one tumor population. Normal cells and other malignant populations can retain the allele and contribute reads. Thus a weak or indeterminate call is not proof of retention. Likewise, a call from one sampled region does not map every lesion.

**Answer:** Both groups, because B\*Y travelled on the same lost haplotype as A\*X. Peptides predicted to bind the retained paternal alleles are not challenged by this finding, but retention alone does not prove they are displayed; that needs presentation evidence.
